title: Is Matter Around Us Pure?
seo_title: Is Matter Around Us Pure? Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 2)
standard_code: Class 9, Chapter 2: Is Matter Around Us Pure?
standard_text: Is Matter Around Us Pure: Elements, compounds and mixtures. Heterogeneous and homogeneous mixtures, colloids and suspensions. Physical and chemical changes (excluding separating the components of a mixture); Pure and Impure substances.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 2: elements, compounds and mixtures, solutions, concentration, suspensions, colloids and the Tyndall effect, and physical and chemical changes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A pure substance has only one kind of particle.
key_sub: Mass % = mass of solute ÷ mass of solution × 100.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pure substances are elements (one kind of atom) and compounds (elements joined chemically in a fixed ratio). Mixtures keep the properties of their parts: homogeneous mixtures (solutions such as salt water and air) are uniform, heterogeneous ones (sand and water) are not.

A true solution has particles smaller than 1 nm and does not scatter light; a colloid scatters light (the Tyndall effect) but does not settle; a suspension settles and can be filtered. Concentration is the amount of solute in a given amount of solution, for example mass by mass percentage.

Example

20 g of salt in 180 g of water. Mass %?

solution = 200 g

20 ÷ 200 × 100

Answer: 10%

Example

Is milk a solution, suspension or colloid?

it scatters light but does not settle

Answer: a colloid

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the mass of the solvent instead of the solution.
  • Calling air a compound.
  • Saying colloids settle like suspensions.

items.q: 5 g of urea is dissolved to make 1,000 mL of solution. What is its mass by volume percentage?
